query: Why are some incidents resolved inefficiently, and which underlying issues drive it?

per_column.name: resolution_days
per_column.rationale: Continuous measure of resolution time; a direct operationalization of resolution_efficiency, i.e., the outcome itself, not a cause.

per_column.name: is_inefficient
per_column.rationale: Binary flag of inefficient resolution -- this is the focus/outcome discretized, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: assignee_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: whether the incident was routed/assigned to the wrong person. Plausibly drives longer resolution and represents an 'underlying issue' whose effect on efficiency is being attributed.

per_column.name: is_critical_or_high
per_column.rationale: Priority plausibly affects both routing/assignment (treatment) and resolution time (outcome); high-priority incidents may be escalated differently and resolved faster/slower, so it is a common cause requiring adjustment.

per_column.name: state_is_resolved
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident reached a resolved state is downstream of the resolution process itself; conditioning on it can induce selection bias, not a legitimate confounder.

per_column.name: above_category_median
per_column.rationale: Defined relative to resolution time within category, so it is essentially a re-expression of the outcome (efficiency benchmarked to category), not an independent common cause.

per_column.name: sys_updated_by_is_employee
per_column.rationale: Type of handler (employee vs. other/automated) can influence both who/how the incident is assigned (treatment) and how quickly it is resolved (outcome), making it a plausible common cause; though weaker and possibly a proxy.

judge.rationale: A clear treatment (assignee_mismatch) is present, and the query names it via 'underlying issues.' The set does surface at least one plausible common cause of both treatment and outcome not stated in the query (is_critical_or_high, i.e. priority), which is the capability under test; sys_updated_by_is_employee is a weaker candidate confounder. However, several added columns are outcome restatements (resolution_days, is_inefficient, above_category_median), one is a likely collider (state_is_resolved), and no strong caller/category/temporal confounders were surfaced. Overall the causal setup is only partially realized, with modest confounder quality.
